questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Switching Two Rows
questions.problem: Suppose $X$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $det(X)=105.$ The matrix $Y$ is obtained from $X$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}↔{R}_{1}$ (switching the first and the third rows). What is the value of $det(Y)?$
questions.worked_solution:
Since swapping any two rows changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite sign, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =-det(X) \\  & =-(105) \\  & =-105.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Multiplying a Matrix by a Scalar
questions.problem: Suppose $Y$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $det(Y)=-3.$ What is the value of $det(4Y)?$
questions.worked_solution:
Multiplying a $n\times n$ matrix by a scalar $k$ is equivalent to multiplying each row by $k,$ and this occurs $n$ times. This leads to the result

$$
\begin{aligned}det(k\cdot Y)={k}^{n}\cdot det(Y).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have $k=4$ and $n=3.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}det(4Y) & ={4}^{3}\cdot det(Y) \\  & =64\cdot (-3) \\  & =-192.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Applying Several Elementary Operations
questions.problem: Suppose $B$ is a $6\times 6$ matrix and $det(B)=-10.$ The matrix $C$ is obtained from $B$ by applying the elementary row operations ${R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{4}↔{R}_{6}.$ What is the value of $det(C)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

- The operation ${R}_{4}↔{R}_{6}$ involves swapping two rows, so it changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.

- The operation ${R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{1}$ involves multiplying a row by $\frac{1}{5},$ so the determinant is multiplied by $\frac{1}{5}$ as well.

Therefore, we have to change the sign of the determinant to the opposite one and multiply by $\frac{1}{5}$ as well. Consequently, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C) & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-det(B)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}det(B) \\  & =-\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-10) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

- The operation ${R}_{6}:={R}_{6}+(-7){R}_{2}$ involves adding a multiple of one row to another row,  so it does not change the determinant.

- The operation ${R}_{1}:=\frac{3}{4}{R}_{1}$ involves multiplying a row by $\frac{3}{4},$ so the determinant is multiplied by $\frac{3}{4}$ as well.

Therefore, we only have to multiply the determinant by $\frac{3}{4}.$ Consequently, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(Y) & =\frac{3}{4}det(X) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot 28 \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying a Row Operation Given the Connection Between Two Determinants
questions.problem:
Given that $det(A)=det(B),$ which of the following elementary row operations transforms matrix $A$ to matrix $B,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & 8 & -2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & -8\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $det(A)=det(B)$, the row operation applied to $A$ must be to add or subtract a multiple of one row to another row. In other words, it is of the form 

$$
{R}_{j}:={R}_{j}+(k){R}_{i},\,i\ne j.
$$

By considering the given row operations that are of the above form, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & 8 & -2\end{aligned}| & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & -2 & -8\end{aligned}| \\  & =det(B).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$
